locked_story.headline: UAF's drone program flew human blood samples 1,000 km out of Nenana on a Windracers ULTRA (8 hours 47 minutes, August 19th), and on November 19th director Cathy Cahill told the Fairbanks chamber rural medical drone delivery is next, with detect-and-avoid radar the key step; Tanana Chiefs Conference and Ryan Air hold first-round Rural Health Transformation grants for drone delivery, and the state's Year 2 award landed November 17th (News-Miner, UAF, Alaska DOH, CMS, ADN)
locked_story.note: Picked independently by three of four researchers, and the fourth surfaced the RHTP funding peg. In-window pegs: News-Miner November 19th, Alaska DOH Year 2 release November 17th. Stance rotation: the last 25 stances are curious or mixed with one cautionary; this is a genuine celebratory story (a thing that works), honestly framed as a test before deployment. The AI angle is robotics and autonomy (an uncrewed aircraft and planned detect-and-avoid), not machine learning, and the film says so. dedupe check FRESH on distinctive entities (first pass collided on the generic tokens air and flight with the 11-19 FAA ground stop, a different subject). Archive overlap noted: 07-03 and 07-20 covered the XPRIZE wildfire finals ACUASI hosted at Nenana, a different subject.

rungs.note: 4 researchers (science/fisheries, energy/defense/UAS, rural/Native/health, wildcard plus primary-source mining incl. NSF API), 76 of 80 WebSearch calls used. All four called it a slow week for Alaska AI news.
